To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. U‐turns play a crucial role in the determination of the backbone topology of globular proteins.

the U‐ turn positions in globular proteins can be predicted with a very high accuracy (94%) using a simple and efficient algorithm that utilizes multiple sequence information and secondary structure propensites, and that both local interactions and global constraints play an important role in determining the secondary structure type between the U‐turns.

1. A new method for predicting the backbone locations where the chain reverses direction (U‐turns) and the dominant types of secondary structure elements (SSEs) between U‐turn positions in globular proteins has been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new and more accurate prediction method for the backbone U‐ turn locations and dominant secondary structure types between the U‐turns (U‐turns are where the chain reverses the global direction).
the development and application of new methods of protein modeling and prediction.
the development of methods for the prediction of protein backbone structure and the prediction of the secondary structure of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current approach provides a significantly better and more reliable prediction of U‐turns and major secondary structural types in proteins, and that it is a significant advance over the earlier method.
the U‐ turns in proteins are not only important for the folding process, they also play a significant role in determining the overall structure of the protein and the stability of the protein fold.
our new approach for predicting U‐turn locations and dominant secondary structure elements is more successful and accurate than our previous method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to predict the secondary structure of proteins with an accuracy of 80% using a simple algorithm based on the amino acid sequence.
we developed a novel method for predicting protein backbone U‐ turn positions and dominant secondary structural elements between them.
our method has been able to provide a very accurate prediction of secondary structure for proteins of all lengths and folds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the U‐ turn locations are primarily determined locally by the interactions between the residues in the U‐turn.
U‐turns are important structural elements in proteins, and that they are primarily determined by the local sequence.

the U‐ turn locations in globular proteins are primarily determined by the local interactions, and that both global length constraints, and local interactions, contribute significantly to the types of secondary structure elements between the U‐turns.
